question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-(5x+\frac{y}{5})}, & x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X\le 5).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $x\ge 0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-(5x+\frac{y}{5})}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[-5{e}^{-(5x+\frac{y}{5})}]}_{y=0}^{y=\infty } \\  & =-5(0-{e}^{-(5x+0)}) \\  & =5{e}^{-5x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}5{e}^{-5x}, & x\ge 0, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 5) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{5}{f}_{X}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}5{e}^{-5x}\text{d}x \\  & ={[-{e}^{-5x}]}_{0}^{5} \\  & =-{e}^{-25}+{e}^{0} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{{e}^{25}}.\end{aligned}
$$
